title: Irregular bundles on Hopf surfaces: the existence of irregular bundles with prescribed weights (Theorem 4)
author: Edoardo Ballico, Elizabeth Gasparim
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the existence theorem for irregular bundles with prescribed weights, printed as Theorem 4 of "Irregular bundles on Hopf surfaces" (source0.tex lines 652--659, source label Wrr7) and announced by the article as item (4) of its introduction, delivered together with the article's own complete proof at source0.tex lines 661--716 (56 lines, one adjacent proof environment). The theorem is one of the article's main results: it produces, for every ordering of the four divisors $D_1,\dots,D_4$, a codimension-2 analytic family of bundles in $\mathcal M_n(0)$ whose first two weights equal 1 and whose last two weights vanish, and, for $n\ge 4$, a codimension-3 family on which the first three weights equal 1 and the fourth vanishes. The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span, and it proves both parts. It first reduces the problem to a statement about the linear system $|\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1}(n,1)|$ by the surjectivity of the graph map (the article's cited Theorem 5.2.2 of Braam-Hurtubise), then uses the retained Proposition 1 to pick a curve $A$ whose second projection has $2n-2$ distinct ramification points with distinct images and uses the unique 3-transitivity of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb P^1)$ to move two of those images onto the points $\pi_2(D_1)$ and $\pi_2(D_2)$; the two ramification points lying over $D_1$ and $D_2$ give a degree-4 subscheme $Z\subset D$, the exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1}\to\mathcal I_Z(n,1)\to\mathcal I_{Z,D}(n,1)\to 0$ together with the K\"unneth formula and the vanishing of $h^1$ on $D\cong\mathbb P^1$ computes $\dim|\mathcal I_{Z,D}(n,1)|$, and the semicontinuity theorem for cohomology of Hartshorne III.13.8 upgrades the count to a whole neighbourhood; transversality to $D_3$ and $D_4$ is an open condition whose failure would force an additional degree-2 contact, and the same exact-sequence count repeated with the degree-6 subscheme $W$ shows that failure locus has positive codimension in the irreducible $\Gamma_2$, giving part (a). Part (b) repeats the construction with three contact points, producing a codimension-3 family $\Delta'$ on which $w_1=w_2=w_3=1$, and then argues by the same dimension count with the degree-8 subscheme $W'$ that the general element of the family is not tangent to $D_4$, which gives $w_4=0$. Every step of both parts is carried out in the retained span; nothing is delegated to another part of the article, and the only external inputs are the article's own Theorem 3 (retained in statement form), its own Proposition 1 (retained), and two cited textbook results (Braam-Hurtubise Theorem 5.2.2 for the surjectivity of the graph map and Hartshorne III.13.8 for semicontinuity), both of which are standard published results named at the point of use. The argument is a research-level deformation-theoretic codimension count over a moduli space of bundles on a Hopf surface, not a textbook exercise: it needs the graph map, ideal-sheaf cohomology on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$, K\"unneth, semicontinuity, irreducibility of the parameter family and the ramification bookkeeping of the spectral construction, and it is the technical core of the article's section on ramifications and weights. It is rated H2 rather than H3 because the proof, although complete, is terse at several points (several steps are taken ``as in step (a)'') and reuses one counting pattern four times rather than introducing a new method.
